To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of integrins and MMP‐9 is up‐regulated in melanoma cell xenografts in mice, and that the up‐regulated expression is associated with the ability of the cells to metastasize.

(1) human melanoma cell tumors growing in nude mice undergo phenotypic and genetic changes similar to those occurring in situ during melanoma progression, including over‐expression of the β3 and β1 integrins and the 92 kDa gelatinase; and (2) the over‐expressed β3 integrin is a potential therapeutic target for the treatment of metastatic melanoma.

the development of a new method for the detection of the 92-kDa gelatinase.

the role of integrin and MMP expression in the development of human melanoma metastasis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of the integrin β3 and of the 92 kDa type IV collagenase (MMP‐9) in melanoma cell tumors in nude mice correlates with the metastatic potential of the cells.

the expression of β3 integrin is not a prerequisite for the metastatic phenotype in human melanoma, as it has been previously proposed, and it does not seem to be an indicator of the invasive capacity of melanoma cells.
the β3 integrins are not the major players in melanoma progression, and that they are not necessarily associated with the invasive and/or metastatic potential of melanomas.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we demonstrated that the melanoma cell line HT‐144, injected into nude mouse, underwent phenotypic changes, similar to those observed during metastasis.
the integrin profile and MMP expression of human melanoma cells can change in vivo, and that this may be an important step during melanoma progression.
integrin expression and MMP‐9 production are not necessarily linked to metastatic potential in vitro.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the expression of integrins, such as β3, and proteolytic activity, such as that of MMP‐9, are not necessarily linked to the metastatic potential of a given tumor cell line, as we observed for SK‐MEL cells.
the integrin β3 and matrix metalloproteinase 9 are over‐expressed in human HT‐145 melanoma cell tumors growing in nude mice.
the integrin β3 and the 92-kDa gelatinase, MMP-9, may be important for the metastatic potential of melanoma cells in the mouse model.
